newsitem.title: USA: Safeco buying American States for $2.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: Safeco buying American States for $2.8 billion.

text.p: In the latest realignment in the insurance industry, Safeco Corp. agreed Monday to pay about $2.8 billion for Lincoln National's American States Financial Corp. subsidiary.
The deal will make Safeco the nation's 12th-largest property-casualty insurer and allow Lincoln National to focus on its life insurance and annuity businesses.

American States' stock leaped $7.25 to $45.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, below the $47-a-share called for in the deal, which has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies. The stock of Lincoln National, which owns about 83 percent of American States' shares, climbed $3.125 to $66, also on the NYSE.
Safeco fell 75 cents to $44.50 on Nasdaq but shares of other property casualty insurers gained on the view that they could become takeover targets in a consolidating insurance industry.

"It indicates how rapidly it's consolidating where companies are getting to the point where they either have to be a buyer or a seller," Lehman Bros. analyst Peter Wade said. "And I suspect Safeco didn't want to be a seller, so they needed to be a buyer."

Among other large takeovers in the industry, Jefferson-Pilot Corp. agreed in February to buy Chubb Corp.'s life insurance business for $875 million and American General Corp. agreed to buy USLife for $1.8 billion. In March broker Marsh & Mclennan Cos. Inc. agreed to buy Johnson & Higgins, another insurance broker, for $1.8 billion.
Safeco said the combined company would have had 1996 revenues of $5.9 billion and will nearly double the number of independent agents that work with either organisation.
Safeco said it expected American States to contribute to its earnings after 1998.

The acquisition will accelerate Safeco's growth east of the Rocky Mountains and strengthen its hand in eight Midwestern and Pacific Northwest states: Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Ohio, Michigan, Kansas, Washington and Oregon.

"The addition of American States to Safeco will result in approximately 4,000 new agents," said Randy Stoddard, senior vice president of Safeco Property/Casualty Insurance Cos., who will become president of the property and casualty operations on July 1.
However, Safeco President Boh Dickey told Reuters that the company expects to reduce the combined work force of about 10,000 by about 5 percent in the next several years, mainly through attrition.
Lincoln National said it will receive about $2.35 billion in cash for its American States' stake and will be repaid $300 million in intercompany American States debt.
It said it will use about $2.15 billion of proceeds from the sale for acquisitions and said its board also authorised the repurchase of up to $500 million of its stock.
The company also said it will seek mutual funds acquisitions where it can broaden its product line, increase distribution and add economies of scale or improve the investment performance.
"When the sale of American States is completed, all of our businesses will be in alignment with our strategy," Lincoln National Chief Executive Ian Rolland said.
In the life insurance sector, Rolland said, the company would consider acquisitions in the United States and Britain. He declined to say if talks were under way.
Since 1990, Lincoln National has made a series of sales and acquisitions in a bid to become a more focused financial services company.
